## Simplicial complexes

A *simplicial complex* $K$ is a collection of simplices (vertices, edges, triangles, ...) closed under taking faces.

## Chains and boundaries

The $k$-chains $C_k(K)$ are formal sums of $k$-simplices with coefficients in a field, usually $\mathbb{F}_2$.
The boundary map sends a simplex to the alternating sum of its faces:

$$
\partial_k [v_0, \dots, v_k] = \sum_{i=0}^{k} (-1)^i [v_0, \dots, \hat{v}_i, \dots, v_k].
$$

The key identity is $\partial_{k} \circ \partial_{k+1} = 0$: a boundary has no boundary.

## Homology

$$
H_k(K) = \ker \partial_k \,/\, \operatorname{im} \partial_{k+1},
\qquad
\beta_k = \dim H_k(K).
$$

$\beta_0$ counts connected components, $\beta_1$ counts independent loops, $\beta_2$ counts voids.
